title: Breadth-first search and shortest paths
summary: Visit the start, then all its neighbours, then theirs: level by level, using a queue.

checkpoints.text: BFS starts at vertex 0: it is marked visited (filled in the graph) and put in the queue.
Vertex 0's neighbours 1 and 2 are found, marked and queued. `parent` remembers who found them: 0.
Next out of the queue is 1, which joined first. Vertices leave in the order they were found, which is why BFS goes level by level.
Vertex 2 looks at 3 (the amber edge), but 3 was already found through 1, so it is skipped. Marking when a vertex is queued stops it being queued twice.
Every vertex was visited once. The order was 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5: by distance from 0 in edges.
Path from 5 back to 0: 5 3 1 0, found by following `parent`. In an unweighted graph BFS always finds a path with the fewest edges. BFS is O(V + E) with lists, O(V²) with a matrix.
